## (c) Harness traps

### Vitest
- **Include glob is `overrides/**/*.test.ts(x)` only** (`vitest.config.ts`). Therefore `scripts/`
  has **no test surface at all** — and widening it means editing a Tier 1 file.
- **`passWithNoTests: true`** — if the glob stops matching (a rename, a moved folder), the suite
  reports success with zero tests. A vacuous-pass enabler baked into config.
- **Does not run Storybook `play` functions.** There is no `@storybook/addon-vitest` /
  Storybook-Vitest integration configured. A `play` is CI-covered *only* via `test-storybook`.
- **No `@salesforce/retail-react-app` alias.** So an override component that imports a *sibling
  overridden* component via the base path silently exercises the **base SFCC** version under Vitest.
  (Same class as the Storybook alias trap; `overrideStyling.md` already documents it.)
- **jsdom always provides `window`.** Any SSR/browser-branch code needs `// @vitest-environment node`
  plus `delete globalThis.window` to reach the server branch.
- **Every `getBoundingClientRect()` is 0 in jsdom.** No geometry, target-size or layout-shift
  assertion belongs at this layer.
- **Vitest cannot load base SFCC `.js` files containing JSX** (`contexts/index.js:49` → "invalid JS
  syntax") and **has no SVG loader** (`icons/index.jsx:79` → `Cannot create property 'viewBox' on
  string`). Both blocked a probe outright; mocking the icons barrel fixes the second, not the first.
- `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/user-event` and `jest-dom` are **in neither
  `dependencies` nor `devDependencies`** — they work purely on npm hoisting, and they are already
  load-bearing for committed test files. A pnpm/nested install breaks the test infrastructure.

### Storybook / `test-storybook`
- **`test-storybook` requires a *built* Storybook.** Pointing it at the dev server produces
  wholesale failures that mean nothing. Build to `storybook-static/`, serve, then test — which is
  exactly what `qa.yml` does.
- **There is no `test:storybook` npm script.** Verified against `package.json`. So the local gate
  cannot be run the same way CI runs it — direct cause of one CI failure and one uninterpretable
  mutation-test run. Adding the script is a `package.json` change (Tier 1, integration approval).
- **`.storybook/main.js` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` straight to `node_modules`** — the
  ccExtensibility resolver is webpack-app-only. A base-path import of an already-overridden
  component renders the **unstyled base** in Storybook while shipping correctly in the app.
- **SFCC SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed** in `.storybook/main.js` (deliberately, mirroring the browser
  build). Consequence: **12 base-template icons render as empty boxes in Storybook** — `bag`,
  `search`, `menu`, `profile`, `close`, `check`, `plus`, `info`, `location`, `password`, `wishlist`,
  `wishlist-selected`. A blank icon in Storybook is not necessarily a bug. Zimmermann-authored icons
  in `zimm.tsx` are unaffected.
- **`.claude/rules/testing.md:87` prescribes `import {...} from '@storybook/test'` — that package does
  not exist in `node_modules`.** Storybook 10 moved it to the `storybook/test` subpath, which is what
  the live footer story actually imports. **Following the ratified rule verbatim produces a
  module-not-found error.** This is a live defect in a Tier 1 policy doc.
- **`testing.md:100` says "never reach into `document` directly"** — but a portalled dialog renders
  outside `canvasElement`, so `within(document.body)` is mandatory for any modal assertion. The live
  story cites a "testing.md §Layer-2 exception" that **does not exist in testing.md**. The rule needs
  the portal carve-out written into it.
- **A `play` *can* assert a Tab trap.** `user-event` checks `defaultPrevented` and skips its own
  focus move, so a trap that calls `preventDefault()` is the only thing that moved focus — the
  assertion is therefore sound. Verified by mutation against a no-trap control.
- **Focus the submit button programmatically, don't click it**, when you need it as the `last` focus
  stop — a click closes the dialog before the trap can be exercised.
- **`extractDescription` in `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` hijacks registry rows.** Demoting one JSDoc
  hands the row to the next declaration — whack-a-mole. A JSDoc on a test/story constant can silently
  become a component's registry description.

### Playwright / measurement
- **`networkidle` never settles on a dev server** (HMR websocket). Use `domcontentloaded`.
- **Programmatic `.focus()` does not trigger `:focus-visible` in Chromium.** A focus-ring test using
  `.focus()` reports no ring on a component that has one. Use real keyboard `Tab`.
- **Hydration race drops keystrokes.** Typing before hydration completes loses leading characters —
  `someone@example.com` arrived as `e@example.com`. Diagnosed as a *test* artefact at
  `asst.txt:10631`; a later, more careful run found it **still reproduces at 25ms/key** on a settled
  page (`test@example.com` → `example.com`, `asst.txt:23800`) and it was carried forward as an
  un-investigated finding, flagged as a likely real UX bug in the controlled-input path. **Latest
  position: unresolved.** Mitigation for tests: focus, wait ~400ms for the label-float transition,
  then `fill()` rather than `type()`.
- **Measure the right element.** A nav underline lives on the inner `<span>`, not the `<a>`.
- **Computed width is not authored width.** Every `width:auto` div reports its used width, so a
  "dimension audit" over computed styles produced 129 meaningless hits. Authored CSS is Phase 2's job.
- **Round before comparing layout floats.** The no-shift assertion uses
  `LAYOUT_PRECISION_DP = 1` + `toFixed` (commit `1bc0a9d`) — sub-pixel jitter otherwise fails a
  correct assertion.
- **Measure after the real font loads.** A 160px column cap calibrated against the fallback stack was
  wrong once Futura Round landed (labels ~12% narrower, so a wrap moved). Fallback resolution is
  **OS-dependent** (macOS resolves system `Futura`, Windows `Century Gothic`, CI generic sans), and
  `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families — so it cannot be used to confirm
  a font is really loaded.
- **Dismiss the consent modal** before screenshotting or measuring; it blocked the viewport centre.

### The hand-list trap (the highest-yield single lesson)
**Phase 1's literal/inline-style checks scanned a hard-coded list of 13 files. `overrides/` has 71.
Seven of the PR's 20 changed files were outside the list — including `header/index.tsx`, the one
file that actually contained the violation being counted.** The reported "7 inline styles" should
have been 8, and the 8th was the only real one (`<ZimmLogo style={{ width: 'min(597px, 60vw)' }} />`).
Phase 2 had the same defect independently (a hand-maintained inventory).

> **Any conformance sweep must be a directory walk over the diff, never a curated file list.** A
> clean report from a scanner that cannot see the offending file is worse than no report.

Related: report **against the baseline, not within the session**. "Inline styles 8→7" was a
within-session delta; against `develop` the count was **0→7**, because every one of those files is
*added* by the PR. There was nothing to improve on.

## (d) CI reality vs appearance — verified live

Required status checks on `develop` (`gh api .../branches/develop/protection`) are **exactly three**:

```
Storybook interaction & a11y tests
Unit tests (Vitest)
🔴 Branch Target Check
strict: true · require_code_owner_reviews: true · required_approving_review_count: 1
```

### 1. Not gated at all — despite existing
- **`npm run lint` / prettier / `npx tsc --noEmit` run in NO workflow.** Grepped all 15 files in
  `.github/workflows/`; the only hits are a path filter on `tsconfig.json` and a prose instruction
  inside `upstream-release-watch.yml`. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide (19 prettier errors
  in `contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and `routes.tsx`, both identical to `develop`) and
  nothing in CI notices. **Typecheck and lint are local discipline only.**
- **`Playwright E2E (localhost)` is not a required check.** Neither is
  `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`, nor any of the four `protected-file-guard` jobs except
  `🔴 Branch Target Check`. The `tier1-guard` warning job is explicitly not a required check by design
  (documented in AGENTS.md); the real Tier 1 gate is CODEOWNERS + branch protection.
- **No CSS bundle budget.** `bundlesize` covers `build/main.js` (180 kB) and `build/vendor.js`
  (550 kB) only. And bundle-size runs only in `deploy-dev`, `deploy-test` and the SIT gate — **never
  on a PR to `develop`**. This PR added two `.woff2` files with no size gate anywhere.

### 2. A named gate that can never fail
`digital-sit.yml`'s `contract-tests` job — *"MuleSoft contract tests"*, `continue-on-error: false`,
a hard `needs` of the `sit-gate` aggregator — runs `npm run test:contracts`, which is:

```
echo 'TODO: MuleSoft contract tests — OpenAPI spec source must be confirmed…' && exit 0
```

It is structurally incapable of failing. Its `success` result is then read by `sit-gate` as a passed
signal. This is the CI-level instance of the integrity principle: **a gate whose name asserts
coverage it does not have.**

### 3. a11y IS gated — the transcript's own correction was wrong
The transcript states 4 separate times that a11y is not gated *"because there is no
`.storybook/test-runner.js`"* (`asst.txt:24665`, correction #13 at `:24695`, and in two summaries).
**That claim is false for the installed toolchain.** Verified:

- `@storybook/addon-a11y@10.4.6` is in `.storybook/main.js` `addons`, and its `preview.js` exports an
  `afterEach` that calls `axe.run` and emits a report (`dist/_browser-chunks/chunk-SL4FEFXY.js`).
  Its `initialGlobals` set `manual: false`.
- `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4` reads that report in `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-402`:
  ```js
  const shouldRunA11yTest = a11yParameter?.disable !== true && a11yParameter?.test !== "off"
      && a11yGlobals?.manual !== true && a11yReport?.result?.violations?.length > 0;
  if (shouldRunA11yTest) { const violations = expectToHaveNoViolations(a11yReport.result);
      if (violations && a11yTestParameter === "error") { rejectWithFormattedError(...); return; } }
  ```
- `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets `parameters.a11y.test = 'error'`.
- `axe-core@4.11.4` is installed.

So **axe violations fail `test-storybook` today, and that job is a required check.** No
`test-runner.js` is needed — that was a Storybook 8 requirement, and the repo moved to Storybook 10
in commit `894ee55`. **The correction was itself an artifact of stale knowledge.** Note the scope
limit that *is* real: this is per-story component-level axe with the Chakra toast regions excluded,
not a page-level or screen-reader pass.

### 4. The real gap: a skipped required check counts as passing
This is the most consequential CI finding, and it is live right now on PR #59:

```
$ gh pr checks 59
Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)      skipping
Playwright E2E (localhost)            skipping
Storybook interaction & a11y tests    skipping   ← REQUIRED
Unit tests (Vitest)                   skipping   ← REQUIRED
…
$ gh api .../pulls/59 → mergeable: true, mergeStateStatus: "blocked"
```

`blocked` is the code-owner review requirement — **not the tests**. Mechanism: `detect-changes` uses
`tj-actions/changed-files` with `since_last_remote_commit: true`, so it diffs against the *previous
push*, not the merge base. The final push contained only `ec9d161`, touching
`.claude/registry/components.md` and `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — neither path is in the
`vitest`, `storybook` or `e2e` allow-lists. All four suites skipped, and GitHub treats a skipped
required check as passing (`qa.yml` says so in its own comments).

Consequence, stated plainly: **a 64-commit, ~5,000-line PR is merge-eligible with zero test
evidence attached to its head SHA.** The trade-off is deliberate and documented in `qa.yml`, but the
practical rule for a reviewer is:

> Before approving, check whether the required suites actually **ran** on the head SHA, or skipped.
> `gh pr checks <n>` shows `skipping` explicitly. A green tick and a skip look the same in the UI
> summary.

Cheapest mitigation available without touching Tier 1 CI: land the final push on a path inside the
allow-lists (any `overrides/**` file), or push an empty-ish `overrides/` touch, so the gates
re-evaluate against the merged state.

### 5. BrowserStack on this PR was a structural no-op
`e2e-browserstack` on a `develop`-targeted PR runs only if a `SFCC-\d+` key is found, scoped by
`--grep @SFCC-NNN`. No spec in the repo carries `@SFCC-55` — the only spec is
`SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`. So even when it ran it would have matched zero tests. Separately it
failed with `Config file does not exist` (pre-existing infrastructure, `.browserstack.yml` is Tier 1
and Integration-owned). Neither state blocks merge, since the job is not a required check.

## (e) Accessibility — the criteria that actually came up, and the patterns adopted

Target is WCAG 2.2 AA. These are the criteria this build exercised repeatedly, with what each
demanded *in practice*.

| SC | Level | What it demanded here |
|---|---|---|
| **2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)** — 24×24 | AA (2.2) | The most-cited criterion of the build. Every interactive control needs a 24px floor. **Do not use `padding` on a Chakra `IconButton`** — Chakra hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a *style prop*, merged after `__css`, so `p: 'xs'` in a theme size is silently discarded and looks like a working 32px target. Use `minW`/`minH`. Final fix: `sizes.icon = { h: 'auto', minW: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', minH: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)' }` (commit `c6fda36`). Also: the 24px floor existed, correctly cited, **on the wrong element** — on the `clearButton` slot with no consumers, while the real submit had no styles. A correctly-cited rule on a dead control reads as coverage. **Where Figma conflicts with 2.5.8, 2.5.8 wins and the delta is documented** (Figma's 23px locale control → shipped 30px, recorded as a deliberate trade). Beware `SC 2.5.5` (AAA, 44px) being mis-cited for a 24px fix — that happened in `200c044` and was silently corrected in `3220239`. |
| **2.4.7 Focus Visible** | AA | Focus rings belong in the theme recipe's `_focusVisible`, never inline. Measured: `1px solid white`, offset `2px`, `:focus-visible` only. Note the corollary in (c): programmatic `.focus()` will not reveal it. |
| **2.5.3 Label in Name** | A | The locale control's visible text is the locale label while its `aria-label` is `"Change locale"` — the accessible name does not contain the visible text. Knowingly accepted by the user for a placeholder shell; **must be revisited when the region selector lands.** |
| **3.2.5 Change on Request** | AAA | Adopted anyway: **a link that opens a new tab must say so in its accessible name.** Implemented as `NEW_TAB_SUFFIX = ' — opens in a new tab'` appended to `aria-label` only when `leavesTheSite(href)` (i.e. `/^https?:/i`). `tel:`/`mailto:` hand off to the OS, so they get **no** `target` and **no** suffix. Paired with explicit `rel="noopener noreferrer"` rather than relying on `target="_blank"` implying it. |
| **1.1.1 / 2.4.4 / 3.2.4** | A | The **inert-but-perceivable** pattern — see below. |
| **1.4.4 Resize Text** | AA | **`rem` for anything that should scale; `px` only for hairline geometry.** A proposed "fix" replacing `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` with `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (48**px**) would have been a WCAG regression — caught only on verification. Also drove S11: a `36px` field height broke the derivation against a `rem` slot, over-reserving 37px at 200% zoom. |
| **2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap / 2.4.3 Focus Order** | A | The modal focus trap. See the hole in (b). |
| **1.3.1 Info and Relationships** | A | `<ul>` with `list-style: none` **drops list semantics in Safari/VoiceOver** — needs `role="list"`. Flagged, one attribute, **not applied** (pre-existing). Still open. Note phases never ran in Safari, so this is exactly the class of issue Chromium-only testing cannot see. |
| **4.1.2 / role semantics** | A | `role="contentinfo"` on the footer; `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` + `aria-labelledby` + `aria-describedby` on the modal; `aria-live="polite"` on the subscribe status region. |

### Patterns worth reusing

**1. Inert-but-perceivable — the correct absent-data pattern.**
When a control has no destination yet (dependency not landed), render a **labelled, non-interactive
`<span>`**:

```tsx
// No destination yet. Kept NON-INTERACTIVE but PERCEIVABLE:
//   - <span>: no href, no tabIndex, so nothing promises an action that cannot be
//     performed (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance).
//   - labelled, not aria-hidden: ZimmIcon emits role="img" + aria-label, so screen
//     reader users learn the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoids the
//     1.1.1 information loss the previous aria-hidden caused).
<chakra.span __css={styles.contactIconLink}>
  <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-label={label} />
</chakra.span>
```

Two failure modes it avoids: a focusable dead control (2.4.4/3.2.4 false affordance) and
`aria-hidden` silence (1.1.1 information loss). **And the recipe must match** — leaving
`cursor: 'pointer'` and `_focusVisible` on an inert span makes it *look* interactive, which is the
same lie in CSS. This was the actual sticking point on the locale control.

**Degradation must be per-channel, not all-or-nothing** — the `ContactChannelFallbacks` story proves
an absent `phoneHref` and an unsafe `whatsAppHref: 'javascript:alert(1)'` both fall back to spans
while a valid `mailto:` still renders as an anchor.

**2. Three absent-data patterns, ranked.** Only the first is correct:
- ① **guard + inert** — correct (`ContactIconRow`).
- ② **fallback-to-empty-string** (`heading ?? ''`) — renders an empty element *with its margins*,
  producing a phantom gap. Wrong: `''` is right for a form *value*, wrong for *content*.
- ③ **silent element swap** (`ZimmNavItem` link → button when `href` fails `isSafeHref`) — changes
  the announced role with no signal. Affected ~18 nav links; dormant only because `#` passes the
  allow-list.

**3. Enforce a11y in the type system where you can.** `ZimmIcon` uses a discriminated union so an
icon must be *either* `aria-hidden` *or* labelled, never both and never neither:
```ts
} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });
// emits role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
```
This is strictly better than a lint rule: it cannot be a vacuous pass.

**4. Security is an a11y-adjacent boundary.** `isSafeHref` gates every anchor in the footer. Final
form after the bypass fix (`1ed34ea`) — note the **normalisation before matching**, which is the
part the original missed:
```ts
const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[�- ]+|[�- ]+$/g;
const TAB_LF_CR = /[	
]/g;
const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
```
Rationale: the WHATWG URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space and removes tab/LF/CR **before**
parsing, and a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`. `/ /evil.com` correctly stays allowed — a plain
space is percent-encoded, not deleted. **When tightening an allow-list, also verify nothing
previously-working is newly rejected** — the check run was "21 anchors and 0 inert-span fallbacks
still rendering at both viewports", because a silent downgrade of a working link to a span would not
surface in any unit test.

### Which layer proves which a11y assertion

| Assertion | Correct layer | Why not elsewhere |
|---|---|---|
| Role, accessible name, `aria-*` attribute, `target`/`rel` | Storybook `play` | Cheapest layer that renders real markup. jsdom-only Vitest works too but you lose the visual |
| Focus order, Tab trap, Escape, focus restore | Storybook `play` | `user-event` respects `defaultPrevented`, so a trap's `focus()` is observable |
| A branch a story structurally cannot reach (e.g. a `disabled`-filter with nothing disabled) | Vitest with a **synthetic harness** | Build a harness with a disabled control at **both** ends of the focus order — otherwise neither wrap fires and the test is vacuous |
| Scroll-lock restoring a **non-empty** prior value | Vitest | A story only ever observes `''` being restored, which is indistinguishable from clearing the property |
| Target size (24×24), layout shift, geometry | Playwright / real browser | **Every rect is 0 in jsdom.** There is currently **no target-size assertion anywhere in the repo** |
| axe rule violations | `test-storybook` (a11y addon) | Already gated; per-story component scope only |
| Screen-reader announcement, Safari list semantics | Manual | Nothing automated covers either |

# Testing, Verification & Accessibility — transferable method from the SFCC-55 footer build

Extracted from the 18–21 Aug 2026 session transcript, then **re-verified against the live repo**
(`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`).
Where the transcript and the repo disagree, the repo wins and the disagreement is called out.

Scope: verification method, verification integrity, mutation testing, harness traps, CI reality,
a11y rules, Playwright pitfalls, layer selection. Tokens/theme, component structure, Figma
geometry and process/workflow are other agents' domains and are only touched where a testing
conclusion depends on them.

---

## (a) The verification method — phases 0–6

The suite was invented mid-build (defined at `asst.txt:11390`, 2026-08-20T06:38) in response to a
user request for eight V&V outcomes. It was then re-run ~6 times over three days. It is **not in
the repo** — it was ad-hoc scripts (`layer1.cjs`, Playwright probes) in a scratch dir. That is
itself the single biggest finding about it: **the most effective checks this build had were the
ones CI cannot run.**

| Phase | Method | What it can prove | What it cannot prove |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0** Gate zero | `npx tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check`, `npx eslint`, `npm test` (vitest) | Compiles, formats, lints, unit tests green | Nothing about rendered output. Both of the build's worst bugs (576px icons, `extendTheme` recipe merge) passed Phase 0 cleanly |
| **1** Static conformance | AST/regex sweep over theme + component **source** | Authoring discipline: raw hex/px literals, `fontSize` vs `textStyle`, bare scale key on a sizing prop, `--zimm-scale-NNN` numerics in JSX, inline `style=` count, compound shorthands, `!important`, dead recipes, `extendTheme` name collisions, style mirrors duplicating a foundation token, base-path imports that silently render unstyled SFCC in Storybook/Vitest, typography-class drift | That the emitted CSS matches the source. And **only the files it was pointed at** — see the hand-list trap below |
| **2** Emitted-CSS provenance | Fetch the real rendered page, parse every rule in the footer subtree | Provenance of all ~336 declarations (51 `--zimm-*`, 33 `--chakra-*`, 36 literals matching a token, 226 structural, **0 undefined vars**). Catches "source looks tokenised but Chakra emitted something else" | Anything not in the DOM at initial render. The subscribe modal's CSS **was never audited at all** because it only mounts on submit (`asst.txt:14172`). Also classifies a compound value containing any `var()` as clean, so `var(--x) solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5)` passes with a raw literal in it |
| **3** Runtime behaviour | Playwright, 20→23 assertions, 3 breakpoints | Hover apply *and* revert, keyboard focus ring, floating label, input retention, empty/invalid submit blocked, modal open + `aria-modal` + focus entry + Escape + focus restore, overlay z-index clears sticky header, no false success | It asserts **current** behaviour, so it locks in whatever state exists — including bugs. See the ContactIconRow case in (b) |
| **4** Figma geometry diff | Playwright measurement vs Figma node metrics, 1440/1280/1023/860/768/375 | Structural padding/gap/breakpoint/anchor deltas — these can and must be exact | Text-derived measurements (label widths, content-hugged columns, wrap points) — **not until the real font loads**, and they differ per OS. Never make a blanket "pixel-perfect ✅" claim while a font is substituted; classify every delta as *geometry / text-derived / real defect* instead |
| **5** Test-coverage assessment | Read what exists, write the gaps, mutation-verify each new assertion | That a specific failure mode now has a regression net | Coverage %, and it cannot tell you a test is *valuable* — only mutation testing does that |
| **6** Review | Local CodeRabbit `cr review --light --base develop`, ×3 | Cross-cutting review against repo guidelines | Stability: **`--light` samples differently each run.** Two Tier-1 majors appeared in run 1 and not runs 2–3 (`asst.txt:13290`). Treat a finding that vanishes as standing, not resolved |

Two ad-hoc checks ran alongside: **axe-core** over the footer (0 violations / 17→23 passes,
wcag2a→wcag2.2aa) and registry-table integrity (208 rows, 0 column mismatches).

### What phases 0–6 explicitly did NOT cover
Stated verbatim at `asst.txt:13308`, and worth re-stating on any future story because a reviewer
will assume the opposite:

- **Production build** — everything ran against the dev server. Matters concretely: `fontFace.tsx`'s
  `assetRoot()` takes a *different branch* under SSR/production (`getEnvBasePath()` + `BUNDLE_ID`).
  That branch was unexercised and had already shipped fonts as HTML once.
- **Storybook `play`** — not run during phases; only the app was.
- **Cross-browser** — Chromium only. No Safari, which is exactly where the `list-style: none`
  list-semantics issue bites.
- **Visual regression** — geometry measured numerically, never pixel-diffed.
- **E2E** — no Playwright spec exists for the footer. Verified: the repo contains exactly **one**
  spec, `e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`. No `@SFCC-55`-tagged test exists.
- **Multi-site** — en-AU homepage only. Not the other 7 storefronts or 11 locales.
- **Live data** — fixture-backed; the Contentful path untested by design.
- **Performance** — no LCP, bundle-size or Lighthouse run, *on a PR that adds two font files*.
- **Manual a11y** — axe is automated only. No screen-reader pass.

### The method's own recommended order of operations
1. Phase 0 first, always — it is the cheapest and it gates the rest.
2. Phase 1 **with a directory walk, never a hand-list** (see (c)).
3. Phase 2 only tells you about what rendered — enumerate the un-rendered states (modals,
   error states, empty states) and say explicitly that they are unaudited.
4. Phase 3/4 need a **settled** page: real fonts loaded, consent modal dismissed, hydration
   complete. A measurement taken before any of those three is not a measurement.
5. Phase 5 last, and every new assertion must be mutation-verified before it counts.

---

## (b) The integrity principle, and every vacuous pass found

> **A check must be made to FAIL on purpose before its pass counts.**

The session's own root-cause statement (`asst.txt:24769`) is the most transferable sentence in the
whole transcript:

> *"In every case the verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it
> verified, and was never made to fail on purpose. Four of them were a **text proxy standing in
> for a directly-available value** — grepping source text to answer a question about a resolved
> runtime object."*

Two derived rules:

- **R1 — Non-vacuity precondition.** Any assertion of the form `expect(offenders).toEqual([])`,
  `forEach` over a collection, or a measured-delta comparison must be preceded by an assertion
  that the input is non-empty / non-zero. Otherwise an empty input satisfies it.
- **R2 — No text proxies.** If the value is available at runtime, read the runtime value. Do not
  grep source text to answer a question about a resolved object.

### Catalogue of vacuous / broken-instrument passes

**Class 1 — assertion that an empty input satisfies**

| # | Instance | Why it proved nothing | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `recipeGuards.test.ts` — 4 guards each `expect(offenders).toEqual([])` | Stubbing `components` to `{}` left **all four green**. The guards asserted absence of offenders, and an empty walk has no offenders | Added `collect() actually walks the registered recipes` asserting `Object.keys(components).length > 0` **and** `collect().length > 0`. Now live in the repo (commit `e686bd3`) |
| 2 | `SubscribePlaceholder` layout-no-shift assertion | Compared height before/after. Proven vacuous in a real browser under **three** collapse modes — `display:none`, `height:0;overflow:hidden`, and an ancestor `display:none` — each measures 0 both times and passes. **Every rect is 0 in jsdom too** | Assert `slotBefore > 0` and `heightBefore > 0` *first*. Live in `footer/index.stories.tsx:236` |
| 3 | First `fontFace.test.tsx` attempt — 5 tests, 2 "green" | The 2 passers did `forEach` over an **empty array**; `cache.inserted` is not how Emotion's `<Global>` surfaces styles. And **jsdom always provides `window`**, so every case took the browser branch — the SSR path (the actual original bug) was never exercised | `// @vitest-environment node` + `delete globalThis.window` + `expect(urls).toHaveLength(2)` as the **first** assertion in every case. Live in `overrides/app/theme/fontFace.test.tsx` |
| 4 | Scroll-lock assertion | Asserting `body.style.overflow === 'hidden'` after open passes even if it was already `'hidden'` | Capture `overflowBefore`, `expect(overflowBefore).not.toBe('hidden')` first, then assert restore against `overflowBefore` rather than `''`. Live in `footer/index.stories.tsx:117` |

**Class 2 — text proxy standing in for a runtime value**

| # | Instance | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Recipe **parity check** (`parts` vs `baseStyle`) via static regex | False-alarmed **three separate times**. `Header` and `ZimmTextInput` have a **function** `baseStyle`, so naive `Object.keys` reports every part missing. Fix: import the recipe and resolve `baseStyle` by calling it |
| 6 | "No story references the clear button" | A **case-sensitive** grep for `"Clear input"`; the story matches `/clear input/i`. The resulting change broke CI (Storybook 1 of 73 failed) |
| 7 | "5 CodeRabbit threads open" | Used REST *"has no reply"* as a proxy for unresolved. Actual: 4. Only GraphQL `reviewThreads.isResolved` answers this |
| 8 | "`cssTextStyles` went 7→5 presets" | Regex `^    [a-zA-Z]+: \{` cannot match `body2`/`heading3` (digits). There were always 7. Nearly reported a non-existent live bug |
| 9 | `trailing` prop "has zero story coverage" | It is covered transitively by 3 `play` functions in `ZimmInputAction`. A prop-vs-story grep reported a proxy as a finding. **A slot prop tested through its consumer is the correct level** |
| 10 | Layer-2 "4 undefined `var()`" | Extraction regex lacked the `i` flag, so `--chakra-lineHeights-normal` truncated at the uppercase `H`. All four were defined |
| 11 | Phase 2 literal count 19→41 | Counted JSX `{/* */}` comment prose, and matched `.rem`/`.em` inside `removeEventListener`/`email` |
| 12 | "1a count 16→24" alarm | A display artefact — one sweep truncated its list. Per-file comparison showed identical counts |

**Class 3 — a green test that encodes the bug as correct**

| # | Instance | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | Phase 3 `✅ contact icons are not focusable` | Passed because `ContactIconRow` was rendered with **no props**, so there were no hrefs to focus — "a green test hiding a cut wire" (`asst.txt:15120`). When real hrefs landed the suite dropped to 19/20, i.e. **the test would have had to be weakened to accept the fix** |
| 14 | Phase 3 `✅ locale button present but inert` | Stayed green whether the control was inert-by-omission or genuinely `disabled` — two materially different a11y behaviours. "The suite won't catch this reverting your decision" (`asst.txt:14686`) |
| 15 | `safeHref.test.ts` reported as *"well covered, 3 layers"* | **13 committed cases, zero backslashes and zero control characters** — while a live bypass (`/\example.com`, `/\t/`, `/\n/`, `/\r/`) sat open in a CodeRabbit finding 6 hours old. "The regex and the tests came out of the same mental model, so the tests could never have found this" (`asst.txt:24360`). The file had been touched 3× since and the bypass survived all three |

**Class 4 — broken instrument / invalid target**

| # | Instance | Rule it establishes |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | `test-storybook` aimed at the **dev** server, twice | The baseline itself failed, making all four mutation results uninterpretable. **`test-storybook` requires a *built* Storybook** (`build-storybook` → static server). After ~15 rapid file mutations a dev bundle is unreliable |
| 17 | `perl -pi` mutation for compound-shorthand guard "passed" | `perl -pi` is line-mode and cannot match `\n`, so the mutation was never applied. Redone in Python |
| 18 | Mutation test using a **stash** to get a baseline | `git stash` reverts to HEAD, not to `develop`. Re-verified by diffing the two files directly against `origin/develop` |
| 19 | Direct `css()(theme)` assertions | **`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`.** So a test that imports the theme and calls `css(...)(theme)` gets every token back **unresolved** — even Chakra's own `space.4`. It looks like it is asserting resolved CSS and is not. Wrap in `toCSSVar(theme)`, or render through a provider |
| 20 | "Reported 0 lint problems" | The grep was broken by ANSI colour codes; actual was 5. Use `--format json` + a parser |
| 21 | `:417` cited as a source line | The file is 206 lines — it was a **bundle offset**, not a source line |
| 22 | A probe that "timed out on `input[type=email]`" | `test-storybook` had already run the story's `play` and submitted the form. Probing a story after its own `play` ran is probing a different DOM |

### Mutation testing as practised here

The bar that emerged, in order of strength:

1. **Baseline must be green on a valid target** before any mutation. If the baseline fails, every
   result is uninterpretable (instance 16).
2. **Reintroduce the exact bug the check was written for** — not a nearby bug.
3. **Orthogonal mutation matrix** — the standard actually achieved by the modal work
   (`asst.txt:23912`): each mutation must kill **exactly** the assertion that targets it and no
   other. Worked example:

   | mutation | perm. Tab | perm. scroll | story play |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Tab branch early-return | ✗ ✗ | ✓ | ✗ focus landed on `<body>` |
   | `overflow='hidden'` write removed | ✓ ✓ | ✗ | ✗ expected `''` to be `'hidden'` |
   | `disabled` filter removed | ✗ ✗ | ✓ | n/a |

4. **CONTROL cases** — deliberate false-positive inputs proving the check is not simply always
   green. S3's responsive-container walker scored 18/18 with **10 deliberate false-positive
   controls**, including Chakra's own `sizes: {md, lg}` recipe shape which must *not* read as
   responsive.
5. **Prove the harness is live.** The S10 mutation (`CONTACT_INDENT → 'l'`, watch 4px→20px)
   doubled as proof HMR was actually applying, so "baselines unchanged" was not a stale reading.

**Track record worth knowing:** the 3 original recipe guards were each written *after* a defect had
shipped — 3 for 3. The 3 added in the final review wave protect **0** live instances — 0 for 3
(`asst.txt:24767`). A guard written from reading code you just wrote is a different, weaker artifact
than a guard written from a defect that escaped. The one exception is the non-vacuity precondition,
which raises the validity of every other assertion in the file and so is worth adding regardless.

**And mutation testing is still not sufficient.** The focus trap was mutation-tested in **both wrap
directions** and still had a real WCAG 2.1.2/2.4.3 hole: focus arriving from *outside* the focusable
set (click non-focusable prose → `activeElement` becomes `<body>` → Tab escapes the dialog).
Reproduced empirically at `asst.txt:26641`. **Mutation testing proves your assertions can fail; it
does not enumerate the states you never thought to assert.** Enumerate entry states explicitly.

---

## (c) Harness traps

### Vitest
- **Include glob is `overrides/**/*.test.ts(x)` only** (`vitest.config.ts`). Therefore `scripts/`
  has **no test surface at all** — and widening it means editing a Tier 1 file.
- **`passWithNoTests: true`** — if the glob stops matching (a rename, a moved folder), the suite
  reports success with zero tests. A vacuous-pass enabler baked into config.
- **Does not run Storybook `play` functions.** There is no `@storybook/addon-vitest` /
  Storybook-Vitest integration configured. A `play` is CI-covered *only* via `test-storybook`.
- **No `@salesforce/retail-react-app` alias.** So an override component that imports a *sibling
  overridden* component via the base path silently exercises the **base SFCC** version under Vitest.
  (Same class as the Storybook alias trap; `overrideStyling.md` already documents it.)
- **jsdom always provides `window`.** Any SSR/browser-branch code needs `// @vitest-environment node`
  plus `delete globalThis.window` to reach the server branch.
- **Every `getBoundingClientRect()` is 0 in jsdom.** No geometry, target-size or layout-shift
  assertion belongs at this layer.
- **Vitest cannot load base SFCC `.js` files containing JSX** (`contexts/index.js:49` → "invalid JS
  syntax") and **has no SVG loader** (`icons/index.jsx:79` → `Cannot create property 'viewBox' on
  string`). Both blocked a probe outright; mocking the icons barrel fixes the second, not the first.
- `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/user-event` and `jest-dom` are **in neither
  `dependencies` nor `devDependencies`** — they work purely on npm hoisting, and they are already
  load-bearing for committed test files. A pnpm/nested install breaks the test infrastructure.

### Storybook / `test-storybook`
- **`test-storybook` requires a *built* Storybook.** Pointing it at the dev server produces
  wholesale failures that mean nothing. Build to `storybook-static/`, serve, then test — which is
  exactly what `qa.yml` does.
- **There is no `test:storybook` npm script.** Verified against `package.json`. So the local gate
  cannot be run the same way CI runs it — direct cause of one CI failure and one uninterpretable
  mutation-test run. Adding the script is a `package.json` change (Tier 1, integration approval).
- **`.storybook/main.js` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` straight to `node_modules`** — the
  ccExtensibility resolver is webpack-app-only. A base-path import of an already-overridden
  component renders the **unstyled base** in Storybook while shipping correctly in the app.
- **SFCC SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed** in `.storybook/main.js` (deliberately, mirroring the browser
  build). Consequence: **12 base-template icons render as empty boxes in Storybook** — `bag`,
  `search`, `menu`, `profile`, `close`, `check`, `plus`, `info`, `location`, `password`, `wishlist`,
  `wishlist-selected`. A blank icon in Storybook is not necessarily a bug. Zimmermann-authored icons
  in `zimm.tsx` are unaffected.
- **`.claude/rules/testing.md:87` prescribes `import {...} from '@storybook/test'` — that package does
  not exist in `node_modules`.** Storybook 10 moved it to the `storybook/test` subpath, which is what
  the live footer story actually imports. **Following the ratified rule verbatim produces a
  module-not-found error.** This is a live defect in a Tier 1 policy doc.
- **`testing.md:100` says "never reach into `document` directly"** — but a portalled dialog renders
  outside `canvasElement`, so `within(document.body)` is mandatory for any modal assertion. The live
  story cites a "testing.md §Layer-2 exception" that **does not exist in testing.md**. The rule needs
  the portal carve-out written into it.
- **A `play` *can* assert a Tab trap.** `user-event` checks `defaultPrevented` and skips its own
  focus move, so a trap that calls `preventDefault()` is the only thing that moved focus — the
  assertion is therefore sound. Verified by mutation against a no-trap control.
- **Focus the submit button programmatically, don't click it**, when you need it as the `last` focus
  stop — a click closes the dialog before the trap can be exercised.
- **`extractDescription` in `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` hijacks registry rows.** Demoting one JSDoc
  hands the row to the next declaration — whack-a-mole. A JSDoc on a test/story constant can silently
  become a component's registry description.

### Playwright / measurement
- **`networkidle` never settles on a dev server** (HMR websocket). Use `domcontentloaded`.
- **Programmatic `.focus()` does not trigger `:focus-visible` in Chromium.** A focus-ring test using
  `.focus()` reports no ring on a component that has one. Use real keyboard `Tab`.
- **Hydration race drops keystrokes.** Typing before hydration completes loses leading characters —
  `someone@example.com` arrived as `e@example.com`. Diagnosed as a *test* artefact at
  `asst.txt:10631`; a later, more careful run found it **still reproduces at 25ms/key** on a settled
  page (`test@example.com` → `example.com`, `asst.txt:23800`) and it was carried forward as an
  un-investigated finding, flagged as a likely real UX bug in the controlled-input path. **Latest
  position: unresolved.** Mitigation for tests: focus, wait ~400ms for the label-float transition,
  then `fill()` rather than `type()`.
- **Measure the right element.** A nav underline lives on the inner `<span>`, not the `<a>`.
- **Computed width is not authored width.** Every `width:auto` div reports its used width, so a
  "dimension audit" over computed styles produced 129 meaningless hits. Authored CSS is Phase 2's job.
- **Round before comparing layout floats.** The no-shift assertion uses
  `LAYOUT_PRECISION_DP = 1` + `toFixed` (commit `1bc0a9d`) — sub-pixel jitter otherwise fails a
  correct assertion.
- **Measure after the real font loads.** A 160px column cap calibrated against the fallback stack was
  wrong once Futura Round landed (labels ~12% narrower, so a wrap moved). Fallback resolution is
  **OS-dependent** (macOS resolves system `Futura`, Windows `Century Gothic`, CI generic sans), and
  `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families — so it cannot be used to confirm
  a font is really loaded.
- **Dismiss the consent modal** before screenshotting or measuring; it blocked the viewport centre.

### The hand-list trap (the highest-yield single lesson)
**Phase 1's literal/inline-style checks scanned a hard-coded list of 13 files. `overrides/` has 71.
Seven of the PR's 20 changed files were outside the list — including `header/index.tsx`, the one
file that actually contained the violation being counted.** The reported "7 inline styles" should
have been 8, and the 8th was the only real one (`<ZimmLogo style={{ width: 'min(597px, 60vw)' }} />`).
Phase 2 had the same defect independently (a hand-maintained inventory).

> **Any conformance sweep must be a directory walk over the diff, never a curated file list.** A
> clean report from a scanner that cannot see the offending file is worse than no report.

Related: report **against the baseline, not within the session**. "Inline styles 8→7" was a
within-session delta; against `develop` the count was **0→7**, because every one of those files is
*added* by the PR. There was nothing to improve on.

---

## (d) CI reality vs appearance — verified live

Required status checks on `develop` (`gh api .../branches/develop/protection`) are **exactly three**:

```
Storybook interaction & a11y tests
Unit tests (Vitest)
🔴 Branch Target Check
strict: true · require_code_owner_reviews: true · required_approving_review_count: 1
```

### 1. Not gated at all — despite existing
- **`npm run lint` / prettier / `npx tsc --noEmit` run in NO workflow.** Grepped all 15 files in
  `.github/workflows/`; the only hits are a path filter on `tsconfig.json` and a prose instruction
  inside `upstream-release-watch.yml`. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide (19 prettier errors
  in `contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and `routes.tsx`, both identical to `develop`) and
  nothing in CI notices. **Typecheck and lint are local discipline only.**
- **`Playwright E2E (localhost)` is not a required check.** Neither is
  `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`, nor any of the four `protected-file-guard` jobs except
  `🔴 Branch Target Check`. The `tier1-guard` warning job is explicitly not a required check by design
  (documented in AGENTS.md); the real Tier 1 gate is CODEOWNERS + branch protection.
- **No CSS bundle budget.** `bundlesize` covers `build/main.js` (180 kB) and `build/vendor.js`
  (550 kB) only. And bundle-size runs only in `deploy-dev`, `deploy-test` and the SIT gate — **never
  on a PR to `develop`**. This PR added two `.woff2` files with no size gate anywhere.

### 2. A named gate that can never fail
`digital-sit.yml`'s `contract-tests` job — *"MuleSoft contract tests"*, `continue-on-error: false`,
a hard `needs` of the `sit-gate` aggregator — runs `npm run test:contracts`, which is:

```
echo 'TODO: MuleSoft contract tests — OpenAPI spec source must be confirmed…' && exit 0
```

It is structurally incapable of failing. Its `success` result is then read by `sit-gate` as a passed
signal. This is the CI-level instance of the integrity principle: **a gate whose name asserts
coverage it does not have.**

### 3. a11y IS gated — the transcript's own correction was wrong
The transcript states 4 separate times that a11y is not gated *"because there is no
`.storybook/test-runner.js`"* (`asst.txt:24665`, correction #13 at `:24695`, and in two summaries).
**That claim is false for the installed toolchain.** Verified:

- `@storybook/addon-a11y@10.4.6` is in `.storybook/main.js` `addons`, and its `preview.js` exports an
  `afterEach` that calls `axe.run` and emits a report (`dist/_browser-chunks/chunk-SL4FEFXY.js`).
  Its `initialGlobals` set `manual: false`.
- `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4` reads that report in `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-402`:
  ```js
  const shouldRunA11yTest = a11yParameter?.disable !== true && a11yParameter?.test !== "off"
      && a11yGlobals?.manual !== true && a11yReport?.result?.violations?.length > 0;
  if (shouldRunA11yTest) { const violations = expectToHaveNoViolations(a11yReport.result);
      if (violations && a11yTestParameter === "error") { rejectWithFormattedError(...); return; } }
  ```
- `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets `parameters.a11y.test = 'error'`.
- `axe-core@4.11.4` is installed.

So **axe violations fail `test-storybook` today, and that job is a required check.** No
`test-runner.js` is needed — that was a Storybook 8 requirement, and the repo moved to Storybook 10
in commit `894ee55`. **The correction was itself an artifact of stale knowledge.** Note the scope
limit that *is* real: this is per-story component-level axe with the Chakra toast regions excluded,
not a page-level or screen-reader pass.

### 4. The real gap: a skipped required check counts as passing
This is the most consequential CI finding, and it is live right now on PR #59:

```
$ gh pr checks 59
Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)      skipping
Playwright E2E (localhost)            skipping
Storybook interaction & a11y tests    skipping   ← REQUIRED
Unit tests (Vitest)                   skipping   ← REQUIRED
…
$ gh api .../pulls/59 → mergeable: true, mergeStateStatus: "blocked"
```

`blocked` is the code-owner review requirement — **not the tests**. Mechanism: `detect-changes` uses
`tj-actions/changed-files` with `since_last_remote_commit: true`, so it diffs against the *previous
push*, not the merge base. The final push contained only `ec9d161`, touching
`.claude/registry/components.md` and `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — neither path is in the
`vitest`, `storybook` or `e2e` allow-lists. All four suites skipped, and GitHub treats a skipped
required check as passing (`qa.yml` says so in its own comments).

Consequence, stated plainly: **a 64-commit, ~5,000-line PR is merge-eligible with zero test
evidence attached to its head SHA.** The trade-off is deliberate and documented in `qa.yml`, but the
practical rule for a reviewer is:

> Before approving, check whether the required suites actually **ran** on the head SHA, or skipped.
> `gh pr checks <n>` shows `skipping` explicitly. A green tick and a skip look the same in the UI
> summary.

Cheapest mitigation available without touching Tier 1 CI: land the final push on a path inside the
allow-lists (any `overrides/**` file), or push an empty-ish `overrides/` touch, so the gates
re-evaluate against the merged state.

### 5. BrowserStack on this PR was a structural no-op
`e2e-browserstack` on a `develop`-targeted PR runs only if a `SFCC-\d+` key is found, scoped by
`--grep @SFCC-NNN`. No spec in the repo carries `@SFCC-55` — the only spec is
`SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`. So even when it ran it would have matched zero tests. Separately it
failed with `Config file does not exist` (pre-existing infrastructure, `.browserstack.yml` is Tier 1
and Integration-owned). Neither state blocks merge, since the job is not a required check.

---

## (e) Accessibility — the criteria that actually came up, and the patterns adopted

Target is WCAG 2.2 AA. These are the criteria this build exercised repeatedly, with what each
demanded *in practice*.

| SC | Level | What it demanded here |
|---|---|---|
| **2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)** — 24×24 | AA (2.2) | The most-cited criterion of the build. Every interactive control needs a 24px floor. **Do not use `padding` on a Chakra `IconButton`** — Chakra hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a *style prop*, merged after `__css`, so `p: 'xs'` in a theme size is silently discarded and looks like a working 32px target. Use `minW`/`minH`. Final fix: `sizes.icon = { h: 'auto', minW: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', minH: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)' }` (commit `c6fda36`). Also: the 24px floor existed, correctly cited, **on the wrong element** — on the `clearButton` slot with no consumers, while the real submit had no styles. A correctly-cited rule on a dead control reads as coverage. **Where Figma conflicts with 2.5.8, 2.5.8 wins and the delta is documented** (Figma's 23px locale control → shipped 30px, recorded as a deliberate trade). Beware `SC 2.5.5` (AAA, 44px) being mis-cited for a 24px fix — that happened in `200c044` and was silently corrected in `3220239`. |
| **2.4.7 Focus Visible** | AA | Focus rings belong in the theme recipe's `_focusVisible`, never inline. Measured: `1px solid white`, offset `2px`, `:focus-visible` only. Note the corollary in (c): programmatic `.focus()` will not reveal it. |
| **2.5.3 Label in Name** | A | The locale control's visible text is the locale label while its `aria-label` is `"Change locale"` — the accessible name does not contain the visible text. Knowingly accepted by the user for a placeholder shell; **must be revisited when the region selector lands.** |
| **3.2.5 Change on Request** | AAA | Adopted anyway: **a link that opens a new tab must say so in its accessible name.** Implemented as `NEW_TAB_SUFFIX = ' — opens in a new tab'` appended to `aria-label` only when `leavesTheSite(href)` (i.e. `/^https?:/i`). `tel:`/`mailto:` hand off to the OS, so they get **no** `target` and **no** suffix. Paired with explicit `rel="noopener noreferrer"` rather than relying on `target="_blank"` implying it. |
| **1.1.1 / 2.4.4 / 3.2.4** | A | The **inert-but-perceivable** pattern — see below. |
| **1.4.4 Resize Text** | AA | **`rem` for anything that should scale; `px` only for hairline geometry.** A proposed "fix" replacing `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` with `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (48**px**) would have been a WCAG regression — caught only on verification. Also drove S11: a `36px` field height broke the derivation against a `rem` slot, over-reserving 37px at 200% zoom. |
| **2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap / 2.4.3 Focus Order** | A | The modal focus trap. See the hole in (b). |
| **1.3.1 Info and Relationships** | A | `<ul>` with `list-style: none` **drops list semantics in Safari/VoiceOver** — needs `role="list"`. Flagged, one attribute, **not applied** (pre-existing). Still open. Note phases never ran in Safari, so this is exactly the class of issue Chromium-only testing cannot see. |
| **4.1.2 / role semantics** | A | `role="contentinfo"` on the footer; `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` + `aria-labelledby` + `aria-describedby` on the modal; `aria-live="polite"` on the subscribe status region. |

### Patterns worth reusing

**1. Inert-but-perceivable — the correct absent-data pattern.**
When a control has no destination yet (dependency not landed), render a **labelled, non-interactive
`<span>`**:

```tsx
// No destination yet. Kept NON-INTERACTIVE but PERCEIVABLE:
//   - <span>: no href, no tabIndex, so nothing promises an action that cannot be
//     performed (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance).
//   - labelled, not aria-hidden: ZimmIcon emits role="img" + aria-label, so screen
//     reader users learn the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoids the
//     1.1.1 information loss the previous aria-hidden caused).
<chakra.span __css={styles.contactIconLink}>
  <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-label={label} />
</chakra.span>
```

Two failure modes it avoids: a focusable dead control (2.4.4/3.2.4 false affordance) and
`aria-hidden` silence (1.1.1 information loss). **And the recipe must match** — leaving
`cursor: 'pointer'` and `_focusVisible` on an inert span makes it *look* interactive, which is the
same lie in CSS. This was the actual sticking point on the locale control.

**Degradation must be per-channel, not all-or-nothing** — the `ContactChannelFallbacks` story proves
an absent `phoneHref` and an unsafe `whatsAppHref: 'javascript:alert(1)'` both fall back to spans
while a valid `mailto:` still renders as an anchor.

**2. Three absent-data patterns, ranked.** Only the first is correct:
- ① **guard + inert** — correct (`ContactIconRow`).
- ② **fallback-to-empty-string** (`heading ?? ''`) — renders an empty element *with its margins*,
  producing a phantom gap. Wrong: `''` is right for a form *value*, wrong for *content*.
- ③ **silent element swap** (`ZimmNavItem` link → button when `href` fails `isSafeHref`) — changes
  the announced role with no signal. Affected ~18 nav links; dormant only because `#` passes the
  allow-list.

**3. Enforce a11y in the type system where you can.** `ZimmIcon` uses a discriminated union so an
icon must be *either* `aria-hidden` *or* labelled, never both and never neither:
```ts
} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });
// emits role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
```
This is strictly better than a lint rule: it cannot be a vacuous pass.

**4. Security is an a11y-adjacent boundary.** `isSafeHref` gates every anchor in the footer. Final
form after the bypass fix (`1ed34ea`) — note the **normalisation before matching**, which is the
part the original missed:
```ts
const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[�- ]+|[�- ]+$/g;
const TAB_LF_CR = /[	
]/g;
const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
```
Rationale: the WHATWG URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space and removes tab/LF/CR **before**
parsing, and a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`. `/ /evil.com` correctly stays allowed — a plain
space is percent-encoded, not deleted. **When tightening an allow-list, also verify nothing
previously-working is newly rejected** — the check run was "21 anchors and 0 inert-span fallbacks
still rendering at both viewports", because a silent downgrade of a working link to a span would not
surface in any unit test.

### Which layer proves which a11y assertion

| Assertion | Correct layer | Why not elsewhere |
|---|---|---|
| Role, accessible name, `aria-*` attribute, `target`/`rel` | Storybook `play` | Cheapest layer that renders real markup. jsdom-only Vitest works too but you lose the visual |
| Focus order, Tab trap, Escape, focus restore | Storybook `play` | `user-event` respects `defaultPrevented`, so a trap's `focus()` is observable |
| A branch a story structurally cannot reach (e.g. a `disabled`-filter with nothing disabled) | Vitest with a **synthetic harness** | Build a harness with a disabled control at **both** ends of the focus order — otherwise neither wrap fires and the test is vacuous |
| Scroll-lock restoring a **non-empty** prior value | Vitest | A story only ever observes `''` being restored, which is indistinguishable from clearing the property |
| Target size (24×24), layout shift, geometry | Playwright / real browser | **Every rect is 0 in jsdom.** There is currently **no target-size assertion anywhere in the repo** |
| axe rule violations | `test-storybook` (a11y addon) | Already gated; per-story component scope only |
| Screen-reader announcement, Safari list semantics | Manual | Nothing automated covers either |

---

## (f) Could not verify / open

1. **The phase 0–6 scripts are not in the repo.** `layer1.cjs` and the Playwright probes lived in a
   scratch directory. Every number quoted from Phases 1–4 is unreproducible from the repo alone. The
   only durable artifacts are the 9 vitest files, 12 story files and `recipeGuards.test.ts`.
2. **`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` does not exist**, yet `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` mandates
   running it before any PR touching `overrides/app/components/**` or `theme/components/**`.
   Confirmed absent (the transcript confirms it 3× independently). A mandated gate with no
   implementation.
3. **The 25ms/key character-drop** was diagnosed as a test artefact, then re-observed on a settled
   page and carried forward as un-investigated. I could not resolve which it is without running the
   dev server (prohibited). Treat as an open defect *and* a flakiness source.
4. **The focus-trap containment fix** (3-line branch for "focus arrives from outside the set") was
   identified and reproduced but, as of the transcript's end, **not applied**. `useSubscribeModal.ts`
   should be checked before anyone reuses that hook.
5. **Whether the Storybook a11y gate has ever actually caught anything.** It is wired and required,
   but every reported run was 0 violations, and I did not build a deliberately-failing story to
   confirm end-to-end (that requires a full `build-storybook`). By this document's own principle the
   gate is **unproven, not proven** — making it fail on purpose once is a ~10-minute task and worth
   doing.
6. **Lighthouse/LHCI secrets.** `digital-sit.yml` has a `lighthouse-ci` job, but memory notes record
   the LHCI/E2E secrets as unset, so the SIT gate may not be passable. Not re-verified here.
7. **`sit`/`release` required checks.** I queried `develop` protection only. Whether `release/**`
   requires the SIT gate is unverified.

---

## Recommended additions to `.claude/rules/testing.md`

Ordered by value. Items 1–3 are corrections to things the file gets wrong today.

1. **Fix the import**: `storybook/test`, not `@storybook/test` (line 87). The prescribed package is
   not installed.
2. **Add the portal carve-out** to "never reach into `document` directly" (line 100) — a portalled
   dialog requires `within(document.body)`. The live code already cites an exception that isn't there.
3. **State what each harness does not run**: Vitest does not run `play`; `test-storybook` needs a
   *built* Storybook; jsdom reports every rect as 0; jsdom always provides `window`.
4. **Add the integrity principle as a hard rule**: every new assertion must be shown to fail on
   purpose before it is committed, and any `toEqual([])` / `forEach` / delta-comparison assertion
   needs a non-empty/non-zero precondition first.
5. **Add "no text proxies"**: read the runtime value, not the source text.
6. **Note that a skipped required check counts as passing**, and that reviewers should check
   `gh pr checks` for `skipping` before approving.
7. **Record that lint, prettier and `tsc --noEmit` are not CI-gated** — so the pre-commit discipline
   in AGENTS.md is the only enforcement.
8. **Record that `contract-tests` is a stub that cannot fail**, so the SIT gate's green is
   three signals, not four.
9. **Add a target-size layer rule**: SC 2.5.8 must be asserted in a real browser; there is currently
   no such assertion anywhere in the repo.

Findings written to `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/f5f727b4-7546-4aa6-9d86-ef229e247d3f/scratchpad/agent-testing.md` (501 lines).

## Highest-confidence, highest-impact findings

**1. The transcript's own a11y correction is wrong — a11y IS gated.** The session concluded 4× that "a11y is not gated, no `.storybook/test-runner.js`" (`asst.txt:24665`, correction #13 at `:24695`, plus two summaries). That was Storybook 8 knowledge. Verified live: `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-402` reads `parameters.a11y.test` and rejects when `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets exactly that; `addon-a11y@10.4.6`'s preview runs `axe.run` with `initialGlobals.manual: false`; `axe-core@4.11.4` installed. No `test-runner.js` needed. **Do not remove that `preview.tsx` a11y block.** Caveat: never made to fail on purpose, so by the session's own standard it is unproven.

**2. A skipped required check counts as passing — live on PR #59 right now.** `gh pr checks 59` shows **all four suites `skipping`**, including both required checks (Vitest, Storybook a11y), yet `mergeable: true` (`blocked` is only the code-owner review). Cause: `detect-changes` uses `since_last_remote_commit: true`, and the final push (`ec9d161`) touched only `.claude/registry/components.md` + `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — outside every allow-list. A 64-commit, ~5,000-line PR is merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**. Reviewers must run `gh pr checks` and look for `skipping`.

**3. Lint, prettier and `tsc --noEmit` are gated nowhere.** Grepped all 15 workflows: no hits. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide (19 pre-existing prettier errors) and CI never notices. Also: no CSS bundle budget, and `bundlesize` never runs on a PR to `develop`.

**4. `digital-sit.yml`'s "MuleSoft contract tests" cannot fail** — `npm run test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0`, and it's a hard `needs` of `sit-gate`. A named gate asserting coverage it doesn't have.

**5. `.claude/rules/testing.md:87` prescribes a package that isn't installed.** `@storybook/test` is absent from `node_modules`; Storybook 10 moved it to `storybook/test`, which the live footer story imports. Following the Tier 1 rule verbatim breaks. Line 100 ("never reach into `document`") also lacks the portal carve-out that portalled dialogs require.

**6. The integrity principle, with 22 catalogued instances.** Root cause verbatim (`asst.txt:24769`): *"the verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was never made to fail on purpose."* Sharpest cases: `recipeGuards`' four guards all stayed green with `components` stubbed to `{}`; the layout-no-shift assertion passed vacuously under three collapse modes and every jsdom rect is 0; `safeHref.test.ts` was reported "well covered, 3 layers" with **13 cases and zero backslashes** while a live bypass sat open. Both fixes are now committed (`e686bd3`, `1bc0a9d`).

**7. Green tests that encode bugs as correct.** `✅ contact icons are not focusable` passed because there were no hrefs to focus; wiring them correctly *dropped* the suite to 19/20. Same shape for `✅ locale button inert`, green whether inert-by-omission or genuinely `disabled`.

**8. Mutation testing is necessary, not sufficient.** The focus trap was mutation-tested in both wrap directions and still let focus escape the `aria-modal` dialog when it arrived from outside the focusable set (reproduced, `asst.txt:26641`) — **fix identified but not applied**. The bar reached elsewhere: orthogonal matrices where each mutation kills exactly one assertion, plus deliberate false-positive controls.

Also: `test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook (dev-server runs made four mutation results uninterpretable); `extendTheme` doesn't populate `theme.__cssMap`, so direct `css()(theme)` assertions pass vacuously; the only e2e spec in the repo is `SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`, so `@SFCC-55` BrowserStack scoping matched zero tests.
